page.layout: One page of text, running head at top; a short verse elegy with a title block and an epicedium heading; the page is cut off at the foot. No margin notes.

l.i: Quem prima excepit chara cum Vxore Geneua
Et fouit, belli tam tum haud ignara futuri:
Sed tuus ipse tibi natus, feruatus & idem,
Rex Henrice, tibi sese deuouerat Vni.
Quae nunc Vota Vides ipsa tibi morte soluta.
Hactenus illa. Tibi sint autem cetera cura,
Lanoum quicunque paras ornare sepulcro.
Nempe cani Virtus pietasque Aeneia
Versi Meruit Maronis Vnico:
Euge, aliquem, Veri afflatum sed numinis aura
Reddat Maronem Mantua:
Quem laudes, Lanoe, tuas, tua dicere facta
Fas gloria sinat tua.
Quid tamen insano iuuat indulgere labori,
Inanibusque iurgiis?
Quid laudes, Lanoe, tuas, tua dicere facta
Certamus, o, Vatum chori?
Carmina quid faciat? promittut carmina famā,
Aeternitatem carmina:
Ipsa canit populos Lanoum FAMA per omnes,
Parentat ipsa AETERNITAS.

page.notes: Right edge is cut and several words are damaged; the first line of the verse, the elegy opening and the line ending "IN" are partly lost. Doubtful readings: "promittut" and "Versi", "famā" and "Vatum" are read with uncertainty. The large initial N of the elegy is written as a plain letter. Greek and italic capitals in the title are as printed where legible.
